subject: maths
title: Perimeter
seo_title: Year 3 Perimeter Worksheets: Squared Grids, Rectangles, Missing Sides and Word Problems
standard_text: Measure the perimeter of simple 2-D shapes.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 perimeter worksheets for the National Curriculum: count round shapes on a centimetre grid, add side lengths in cm and m, rectangles and squares, missing sides and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Perimeter is the distance all the way round a shape. Add every side.
key_sub: A rectangle has 4 sides, even when only 2 numbers are shown. On a grid, count the 1 cm sides round the edge, not the squares. Keep the same unit as the sides: cm or m.
body_html:
What is perimeter?

The perimeter is the distance all the way round the edge of a flat shape. Imagine an ant walking round the edge until it gets back to the start. Perimeter is a length, so we measure it in cm or m.

Perimeter on a centimetre grid

Each square has sides of 1 cm. Count the sides of the squares round the edge, not the squares.

Add all the sides

When the sides are labelled, add every side. Touch each side as you add it, so you do not miss one.

Rectangles and squares

Opposite sides of a rectangle are the same length. A picture may show only 2 numbers, but a rectangle has 4 sides. A square has 4 sides the same length.

Example

A square has sides of 6 m. What is its perimeter?

6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24. Or use the 4 times table: 4 × 6 = 24.

Answer: 24 m

Find a missing side

If you know the perimeter, add the sides you know. Then take that away from the perimeter.

Example

A triangle has a perimeter of 20 cm. Two sides are 6 cm and 8 cm. How long is the third side?

6 + 8 = 14. 20 − 14 = 6.

Answer: 6 cm

Example

A rectangle has a perimeter of 18 m. It is 5 m long. How wide is it?

Two long sides: 5 + 5 = 10. 18 − 10 = 8 for the two short sides. Half of 8 is 4.

Answer: 4 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the squares inside (15)Count the 1 cm sides round the edge (16 cm)
Counting the squares round the edge (12)A corner square has 2 sides on the edge
Adding only the 2 numbers shown (9 + 4 = 13)A rectangle has 4 sides: 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26
Counting a corner twice when counting dotsCount the sides between the dots, not the dots
Writing m when the sides are in cmUse the same unit as the sides

faq.q: What is perimeter in Year 3 maths?
faq.a: Perimeter is the distance all the way round the edge of a flat shape. Year 3 children find it by adding the lengths of all the sides, in centimetres or metres.

faq.q: How do you find the perimeter of a rectangle?
faq.a: Add all 4 sides. Opposite sides are the same, so a rectangle 9 cm by 4 cm has a perimeter of 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 cm.
No. In the National Curriculum, Year 3 measures perimeter. Area by counting squares starts in Year 4.

faq.q: How do you find perimeter on a squared grid?
faq.a: If each square has sides of 1 cm, count the sides of the squares round the outside of the shape. Do not count the squares inside.

items.q: A rabbit run is 6 m long and 4 m wide. One long side is against a wall, so it needs no fence. How much fence is needed for the other sides?

items.q: Oliver’s family puts a fence round their garden. The garden is a rectangle 9 m long and 6 m wide. How much fence do they need?
items.e: The fence goes along all 4 sides: 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 m. 15 m is only two sides.

items.q: Jack makes a rectangle with 30 cm of string. The rectangle is 9 cm long. How wide is it?
items.e: The two long sides use 9 + 9 = 18 cm. 30 − 18 = 12 cm is left for the two short sides. Half of 12 is 6 cm.

items.q: Freya puts a paper border round a display board. The board is 150 cm long and 100 cm wide. How long is the border?

items.q: A vegetable patch is 8 m long and 5 m wide. A fence goes all the way round, but there is a gate 1 m wide. How much fence is needed?

items.q: A square tablecloth has sides of 90 cm. Grandma sews lace round the edge. How much lace does she need?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 90 + 90 + 90 + 90 = 360 cm. (4 × 9 = 36, so 4 × 90 = 360.)

items.q: A road sign is a pentagon. Each side is 20 cm. Aisha puts tape round the edge. How much tape does she use?

items.q: Amelia sticks ribbon round the edge of a birthday card. The card is 15 cm long and 10 cm wide. How much ribbon does she need?

items.q: Noah has 1 m of ribbon. He puts ribbon round a card that is 20 cm long and 10 cm wide. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Perimeter of the card: 20 + 10 + 20 + 10 = 60 cm. Left: 100 − 60 = 40 cm.

items.q: A rug is 2 m long and 1 m wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6 m. The sides are in metres, so the perimeter is in metres, not cm.

items.q: Leo wants to find the perimeter of the school field. Which unit should he use?
items.e: A field is big, so measure it in metres. Perimeter is a length, so it is never in litres.

items.q: Ava wants to find the perimeter of a bookmark. Which unit should she use?
items.e: A bookmark is small, so measure it in centimetres. Perimeter is a length, so it is not in kilograms.

items.q: The school playground is a rectangle 40 m long and 25 m wide. Harry walks once round the edge. How far does he walk?
items.e: Once round is the perimeter: 40 + 25 + 40 + 25 = 130 m.

items.q: Poppy walks round a path shaped like a triangle. Its sides are 30 m, 40 m and 50 m. Arjun walks round a square path with sides of 35 m. Who walks further?
items.e: Poppy: 30 + 40 + 50 = 120 m. Arjun: 35 + 35 + 35 + 35 = 140 m. 140 − 120 = 20 m, so Arjun walks 20 m further.

items.q: A square garden has sides of 8 m. Fence panels are 2 m long. How many panels go all the way round?
items.e: Perimeter: 8 + 8 + 8 + 8 = 32 m. Each panel is 2 m: 32 ÷ 2 = 16 panels.
